playable character, and his young son,

nine realms. Kratos keeps his 
troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world.

battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in

Norse mythology, with the majority of it set in mythical ancient 
Scandinavia in the realm of

Kratos, the former Greek God of War who remains the only 
playable character, and his young son, 
Atreus. Following the death of Kratos's second wife and Atreus's mother, Faye, the two embark on a deeply personal journey to fulfill her request that her ashes be spread from the highest peak of the 
nine realms. Kratos keeps his 
troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world.

Cory Barlog as a reimagining of the franchise, a major 
gameplay change is that Kratos makes prominent use of a magical 
battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in 
one shot, as opposed to the

Windows port released in January 2022. It is the eighth installment in the 
God of War series, the eighth chronologically, and the sequel to 2010's 
God of War III. 
Unlike previous games, which were loosely based on 
Greek mythology, this installment transitioned the series to 
Norse mythology, with the majority of it set in mythical ancient 
Scandinavia in the realm of 
Midgard. For the first time in the series, there are two protagonists: 
Kratos, the former Greek God of War who remains the only 
playable character, and his young son, 
Atreus. Following the death of Kratos's second wife and Atreus's mother, Faye, the two embark on a deeply personal journey to fulfill her request that her ashes be spread from the highest peak of the 
nine realms. Kratos keeps his 
troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world. 
Described by creative director

battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in

God of War[b] is a 2018 
action-adventure game developed by 
Santa Monica Studio and published by 
Sony Interactive Entertainment. The game was released worldwide for the 
PlayStation 4 in April 2018, with a 
Windows port released in January 2022. It is the eighth installment in the 
God of War series, the eighth chronologically, and the sequel to 2010's 
God of War III. 
Unlike previous games, which were loosely based on 
Greek mythology, this installment transitioned the series to 
Norse mythology, with the majority of it set in mythical ancient 
Scandinavia in the realm of 
Midgard. For the first time in the series, there are two protagonists: 
Kratos, the former Greek God of War who remains the only 
playable character, and his young son, 
Atreus. Following the death of Kratos's second wife and Atreus's mother, Faye, the two embark on a deeply personal journey to fulfill her request that her ashes be spread from the highest peak of the 
nine realms. Kratos keeps his 
troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world. 
Described by creative director 
Cory Barlog as a reimagining of the franchise, a major 
gameplay change is that Kratos makes prominent use of a magical 
battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in 
one shot, as opposed to the 
fixed cinematic camera of the previous entries. It also includes

gods of the Norse world.

God of War[b] is a 2018 
action-adventure game developed by 
Santa Monica Studio and published by 
Sony Interactive Entertainment. The game was released worldwide for the 
PlayStation 4 in April 2018, with a 
Windows port released in January 2022. It is the eighth installment in the 
God of War series, the eighth chronologically, and the sequel to 2010's 
God of War III. 
Unlike previous games, which were loosely based on 
Greek mythology, this installment transitioned the series to 
Norse mythology, with the majority of it set in mythical ancient 
Scandinavia in the realm of 
Midgard. For the first time in the series, there are two protagonists: 
Kratos, the former Greek God of War who remains the only 
playable character, and his young son, 
Atreus. Following the death of Kratos's second wife and Atreus's mother, Faye, the two embark on a deeply personal journey to fulfill her request that her ashes be spread from the highest peak of the 
nine realms. Kratos keeps his 
troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world. 
Described by creative director 
Cory Barlog as a reimagining of the franchise, a major 
gameplay change is that Kratos makes prominent use of a magical 
battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in 
one shot, as opposed to the 
fixed cinematic camera of the previous entries. It also includes

playable character, and his young son,

troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world.

double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an

God of War[b] is a 2018 
action-adventure game developed by 
Santa Monica Studio and published by 
Sony Interactive Entertainment. The game was released worldwide for the 
PlayStation 4 in April 2018, with a 
Windows port released in January 2022. It is the eighth installment in the 
God of War series, the eighth chronologically, and the sequel to 2010's 
God of War III. 
Unlike previous games, which were loosely based on 
Greek mythology, this installment transitioned the series to 
Norse mythology, with the majority of it set in mythical ancient 
Scandinavia in the realm of 
Midgard. For the first time in the series, there are two protagonists: 
Kratos, the former Greek God of War who remains the only 
playable character, and his young son, 
Atreus. Following the death of Kratos's second wife and Atreus's mother, Faye, the two embark on a deeply personal journey to fulfill her request that her ashes be spread from the highest peak of the 
nine realms. Kratos keeps his 
troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world. 
Described by creative director 
Cory Barlog as a reimagining of the franchise, a major 
gameplay change is that Kratos makes prominent use of a magical 
battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in 
one shot, as opposed to the 
fixed cinematic camera of the previous entries. It also includes

troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world.

battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in

God of War series, the eighth chronologically, and the sequel to 2010's 
God of War III. 
Unlike previous games, which were loosely based on 
Greek mythology, this installment transitioned the series to 
Norse mythology, with the majority of it set in mythical ancient 
Scandinavia in the realm of 
Midgard. For the first time in the series, there are two protagonists: 
Kratos, the former Greek God of War who remains the only 
playable character, and his young son, 
Atreus. Following the death of Kratos's second wife and Atreus's mother, Faye, the two embark on a deeply personal journey to fulfill her request that her ashes be spread from the highest peak of the 
nine realms. Kratos keeps his 
troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world. 
Described by creative director 
Cory Barlog as a reimagining of the franchise, a major 
gameplay change is that Kratos makes prominent use of a magical 
battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in 
one shot, as opposed to the

# Task

# Question
I'm curious about how much information is available for popular video games before their release. Find the Wikipedia page for the 2019 game that won the British Academy Games Awards. How many revisions did that page have before the month listed as the game's release date on that Wikipedia page (as of the most recent entry from 2022)?

# Important Constraint
You MUST solve this problem within 50 rounds of conversation. Plan your approach efficiently and focus on the most direct path to the answer.

# Output format (MANDATORY)
Please respond in the following structure:
## ANSWER
[concise final answer]
## REASON
[brief reasoning or evidence used to reach the answer]

If you obtain and output the final answer, please output 'terminate' in **uppercase** format.



To answer this request we have assembled the following team:

FileSurfer: An agent that can handle local files.
WebSurfer: A helpful assistant with access to a web browser. Ask them to perform web searches, open pages, and interact with content (e.g., clicking links, scrolling the viewport, filling in form fields, etc.). It can also summarize the entire page, or answer questions based on the content of the page. It can also be asked to sleep and wait for pages to load, in cases where the page seems not yet fully loaded.
Coder: A helpful and general-purpose AI assistant that has strong language skills, Python skills, and Linux command line skills.
ComputerTerminal: A computer terminal that performs no other action than running Python scripts (provided to it quoted in ```python code blocks), or sh shell scripts (provided to it quoted in ```sh code blocks).


Here is an initial fact sheet to consider:

1. GIVEN OR VERIFIED FACTS
   - The question is about a video game from 2019 that won the British Academy Games Awards.

2. FACTS TO LOOK UP
   - The winner of the British Academy Games Awards for the year 2019.
   - The release date of the winning game as listed on its Wikipedia page.
   - The Wikipedia revision history of the winning game's page before the release date.
   - The most recent Wikipedia entry from 2022 for the winning game.

3. FACTS TO DERIVE
   - The number of Wikipedia revisions before the game's release date, given the most recent information from 2022.

4. EDUCATED GUESSES
   - The game "Outer Wilds" might be the one, as it is known for winning awards in 2019.
   - Most popular games have a significant number of Wikipedia revisions prior to their release due to public interest and ongoing updates.



Here is the plan to follow as best as possible:

- Use WebSurfer to look up the winner of the British Academy Games Awards for the year 2019.
- Once identified, find the Wikipedia page of the winning game using WebSurfer.

God of War[b] is a 2018 
action-adventure game developed by 
Santa Monica Studio and published by 
Sony Interactive Entertainment. The game was released worldwide for the 
PlayStation 4 in April 2018, with a 
Windows port released in January 2022. It is the eighth installment in the 
God of War series, the eighth chronologically, and the sequel to 2010's 
God of War III. 
Unlike previous games, which were loosely based on 
Greek mythology, this installment transitioned the series to 
Norse mythology, with the majority of it set in mythical ancient 
Scandinavia in the realm of 
Midgard. For the first time in the series, there are two protagonists: 
Kratos, the former Greek God of War who remains the only 
playable character, and his young son, 
Atreus. Following the death of Kratos's second wife and Atreus's mother, Faye, the two embark on a deeply personal journey to fulfill her request that her ashes be spread from the highest peak of the 
nine realms. Kratos keeps his 
troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world. 
Described by creative director 
Cory Barlog as a reimagining of the franchise, a major 
gameplay change is that Kratos makes prominent use of a magical 
battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in 
one shot, as opposed to the

God of War series, the eighth chronologically, and the sequel to 2010's 
God of War III. 
Unlike previous games, which were loosely based on 
Greek mythology, this installment transitioned the series to 
Norse mythology, with the majority of it set in mythical ancient 
Scandinavia in the realm of 
Midgard. For the first time in the series, there are two protagonists: 
Kratos, the former Greek God of War who remains the only 
playable character, and his young son, 
Atreus. Following the death of Kratos's second wife and Atreus's mother, Faye, the two embark on a deeply personal journey to fulfill her request that her ashes be spread from the highest peak of the 
nine realms. Kratos keeps his 
troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world. 
Described by creative director 
Cory Barlog as a reimagining of the franchise, a major 
gameplay change is that Kratos makes prominent use of a magical 
battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in 
one shot, as opposed to the

Norse mythology, with the majority of it set in mythical ancient 
Scandinavia in the realm of 
Midgard. For the first time in the series, there are two protagonists: 
Kratos, the former Greek God of War who remains the only 
playable character, and his young son, 
Atreus. Following the death of Kratos's second wife and Atreus's mother, Faye, the two embark on a deeply personal journey to fulfill her request that her ashes be spread from the highest peak of the 
nine realms. Kratos keeps his 
troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world. 
Described by creative director 
Cory Barlog as a reimagining of the franchise, a major 
gameplay change is that Kratos makes prominent use of a magical 
battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in 
one shot, as opposed to the

   - The question is about a video game from 2019 that won the British Academy Games Awards.

   - The winner of the British Academy Games Awards for the year 2019.
   - The release date of the winning game as listed on its Wikipedia page.
   - The Wikipedia revision history of the winning game's page before the release date.
   - The most recent Wikipedia entry from 2022 for the winning game.

3. FACTS TO DERIVE
   - The number of Wikipedia revisions before the game's release date, given the most recent information from 2022.

4. EDUCATED GUESSES

- Extract the release date listed on the Wikipedia page of the game.
- Access the revision history of that Wikipedia page using WebSurfer to determine the number of revisions made before the release date.
- Count the revisions by analyzing the revision timestamps up to the release date.
- Ensure all information is as per the latest updates available until 2022.

God of War[b] is a 2018 
action-adventure game developed by 
Santa Monica Studio and published by 
Sony Interactive Entertainment. The game was released worldwide for the 
PlayStation 4 in April 2018, with a 
Windows port released in January 2022. It is the eighth installment in the 
God of War series, the eighth chronologically, and the sequel to 2010's 
God of War III. 
Unlike previous games, which were loosely based on 
Greek mythology, this installment transitioned the series to 
Norse mythology, with the majority of it set in mythical ancient 
Scandinavia in the realm of 
Midgard. For the first time in the series, there are two protagonists: 
Kratos, the former Greek God of War who remains the only 
playable character, and his young son, 
Atreus. Following the death of Kratos's second wife and Atreus's mother, Faye, the two embark on a deeply personal journey to fulfill her request that her ashes be spread from the highest peak of the 
nine realms. Kratos keeps his 
troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world. 
Described by creative director 
Cory Barlog as a reimagining of the franchise, a major 
gameplay change is that Kratos makes prominent use of a magical 
battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in 
one shot, as opposed to the 
fixed cinematic camera of the previous entries. It also includes

God of War III. 
Unlike previous games, which were loosely based on 
Greek mythology, this installment transitioned the series to 
Norse mythology, with the majority of it set in mythical ancient 
Scandinavia in the realm of 
Midgard. For the first time in the series, there are two protagonists: 
Kratos, the former Greek God of War who remains the only 
playable character, and his young son, 
Atreus. Following the death of Kratos's second wife and Atreus's mother, Faye, the two embark on a deeply personal journey to fulfill her request that her ashes be spread from the highest peak of the 
nine realms. Kratos keeps his 
troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world. 
Described by creative director 
Cory Barlog as a reimagining of the franchise, a major 
gameplay change is that Kratos makes prominent use of a magical 
battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in

God of War[b] is a 2018 
action-adventure game developed by 
Santa Monica Studio and published by 
Sony Interactive Entertainment. The game was released worldwide for the 
PlayStation 4 in April 2018, with a 
Windows port released in January 2022. It is the eighth installment in the 
God of War series, the eighth chronologically, and the sequel to 2010's 
God of War III. 
Unlike previous games, which were loosely based on 
Greek mythology, this installment transitioned the series to 
Norse mythology, with the majority of it set in mythical ancient 
Scandinavia in the realm of 
Midgard. For the first time in the series, there are two protagonists: 
Kratos, the former Greek God of War who remains the only 
playable character, and his young son, 
Atreus. Following the death of Kratos's second wife and Atreus's mother, Faye, the two embark on a deeply personal journey to fulfill her request that her ashes be spread from the highest peak of the 
nine realms. Kratos keeps his 
troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world. 
Described by creative director 
Cory Barlog as a reimagining of the franchise, a major 
gameplay change is that Kratos makes prominent use of a magical 
battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in 
one shot, as opposed to the 
fixed cinematic camera of the previous entries. It also includes

To achieve this task efficiently, we'll use the Wikipedia API to access the revision history for the "God of War (2018 video game)" page. Then, we'll count the number of revisions made before April 2018. Here's the code to perform this:

```python
import requests
from datetime import datetime

# Definitions
page_title = "God_of_War_(2018_video_game)"
end_date_str = "2018-04-01T00:00:00Z"
end_date = datetime.strptime(end_date_str, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")

# Wikipedia API endpoint for revisions
url = f"https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php"

# Parameters for querying revisions
params = {
    "action": "query",
    "format": "json",
    "prop": "revisions",
    "titles": page_title,
    "rvlimit": "max",
    "rvend": end_date_str
}

def count_revisions():
    # Initialize revision count
    revision_count = 0
    session = requests.Session()
    continue_token = {}

    while True:
        # If there's a continue token, add it to the parameters
        if continue_token:
            params.update(continue_token)

        # Send request
        response = session.get(url, params=params)
        data = response.json()

        # Extract page data
        page_data = next(iter(data['query']['pages'].values()))
        revisions = page_data.get('revisions', [])

        # Increase count based on available revisions
        revision_count += len(revisions)

        # Check for a continue token for more revisions
        continue_token = data.get('continue', None)
        if not continue_token:
            break

    return revision_count

# Execute the function and print the count
revision_count = count_revisions()
print("Number of revisions before April 2018:", revision_count)
```

God of War[b] is a 2018 
action-adventure game developed by 
Santa Monica Studio and published by 
Sony Interactive Entertainment. The game was released worldwide for the 
PlayStation 4 in April 2018, with a 
Windows port released in January 2022. It is the eighth installment in the 
God of War series, the eighth chronologically, and the sequel to 2010's 
God of War III. 
Unlike previous games, which were loosely based on 
Greek mythology, this installment transitioned the series to 
Norse mythology, with the majority of it set in mythical ancient 
Scandinavia in the realm of 
Midgard. For the first time in the series, there are two protagonists: 
Kratos, the former Greek God of War who remains the only 
playable character, and his young son, 
Atreus. Following the death of Kratos's second wife and Atreus's mother, Faye, the two embark on a deeply personal journey to fulfill her request that her ashes be spread from the highest peak of the 
nine realms. Kratos keeps his 
troubled past a secret from Atreus, who is unaware of his 
divine nature. Along their journey, they come into conflict with monsters and 
gods of the Norse world. 
Described by creative director 
Cory Barlog as a reimagining of the franchise, a major 
gameplay change is that Kratos makes prominent use of a magical 
battle axe known as the Leviathan Axe instead of his signature 
double-chained blades called the Blades of Chaos. The game also uses an 
over-the-shoulder free camera, with the game in 
one shot, as opposed to the
